analysis: Both supplied units are context excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines ~418-613 and 613 onward) with no visible diff markers; only documentation prose is present, and no executable source, configuration, or authorization code is in view. The excerpts describe App Attest key rotation (per-machine hourly/daily limits, EIGENINFERENCE_APP_ATTEST_KEY_ROTATION_PERCENT default 100, rotated keys must pass full attestation/receipt/build-qualification/assertion checks and never revoke/deny serving), invalidKey backoff, extra APNs code-identity retries (bounded by the per-device push budget), staged MDA chain for macOS 27 candidates (attached only after hardware trust and re-verified to Apple root), and untrusted ready-reply diagnostics (launch_session, boot_time, operation_stalled_seconds outside the signed transcript; the coordinator drops invalid values and they do not affect authorization). These align with the TB-002 statement that diagnostics are untrusted and with TB-011/T-052..T-058. Described behaviors that the next pass should verify in the actual code, which was not supplied: (1) rotation admission is serialized with machine merges, so overlapping identities cannot bypass budgets (T-055); (2) a rotated key cannot inherit old authorization (T-053/T-054); (3) the coordinator-side diagnostic parsing is bounded and cannot be used to influence authorization; (4) the additional APNs retries stay within the existing push budget (T-023). No concrete security regression is evidenced by the changelog text itself. Coverage limit: the underlying code changes were not available, so no conclusion that they are safe is made.
